growth_004:n1.prompt:
You are helping me set up a customer support platform account as part of standing up our customer support stack (messaging, help center, ticket management). The vendor for this role is {{vendor}} — I will tell you which specific product I've chosen if you don't already know; ask me for it if it's missing, along with my company domain, the email address to use for signup, and any team member names/emails who should be added as agents.

Your job is to PREPARE everything needed to create the {{vendor}} account, but you must NOT submit the signup form, accept any terms of service, or authorize any billing/subscription — that decision requires a human with signing and spending authority.

Please do the following:
1. Navigate to {{vendor}}'s signup page.
2. Fill in the signup form fields (company name, domain, admin email, team size, use case) using the information I provide, without submitting.
3. Identify and summarize the pricing tier(s) that appear relevant to our use case, including any free trial terms.
4. Note any terms of service or data processing agreement links so I can review them.
5. Prepare a checklist covering: account owner email, chosen plan/tier, billing method needed, teammates to invite, and any workspace/subdomain name to reserve.
6. Do not click submit, sign up, agree to terms, or enter any payment details.

When you've completed the form-fill draft and checklist, stop for human sign-off. Report back with: the vendor name used, the prepared form field values, the pricing tier you identified as most relevant and why, links to the terms of service and privacy/data policy, and the full checklist for my review and approval before account creation proceeds.

growth_004:n2.prompt:
You are helping me install the Intercom Messenger widget on my website as part of setting up customer support. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for any missing inputs you need: my website domain, which pages/sections should show the Messenger (e.g., all pages, marketing site only, or logged-in app only), and confirmation that I have an active Intercom workspace using my configured credentials.

2. Using Intercom's dashboard or install documentation, prepare the Messenger installation: retrieve or identify the correct install snippet/method for my site (e.g., generic JavaScript snippet, or platform-specific method if I tell you I use a website builder or framework like WordPress, Shopify, Webflow, React, etc.).

3. Draft the exact code snippet or configuration steps needed, tailored to my stack, including where it should be placed (e.g., before the closing body tag, in a layout file, or via tag manager).

4. Prepare a short checklist covering: where the snippet will be added, which pages it will appear on, any visibility/targeting rules (logged-in users only, specific URLs, etc.), and how to verify it loads correctly (e.g., visiting the site and confirming the Messenger bubble appears).

5. Do NOT apply any changes to my live site, code repository, or CMS. Do not push, deploy, publish, or merge anything.

6. Present me with the finalized snippet, placement instructions, and verification checklist, then stop for human sign-off so I can review and personally apply or authorize the change.

Report back with: the exact snippet/config prepared, the recommended placement location, the verification steps, and a clear note that this remains a human step for actual deployment/approval.

growth_004:n3.prompt:
You are helping me set up the inbox and routing configuration for our customer support tool, {{vendor}}. Before starting, ask me for: (1) the {{vendor}} account/workspace details or confirmation you can access it with my configured credentials, (2) the list of support teams I want created (e.g., Billing, Technical, Onboarding), (3) the channels we support (chat, email, in-app, Slack, WhatsApp, social, etc.), and (4) my handoff rules — the topics, sentiment thresholds, customer tiers, or explicit customer requests that should trigger escalation from the AI agent to a human.

Using this information, please: draft the support team structure to be created in {{vendor}}; draft the automation rules that trigger actions on events (e.g., new ticket, tagged sentiment, VIP customer) so routing happens automatically; draft the handoff conditions so the AI agent reliably escalates per my rules; and note how {{vendor}} will sync tickets and context if it runs inside an existing helpdesk versus standalone, plus which of my required channels it covers natively versus needs a channel integration.

Compile all of this into a single clear configuration checklist showing: teams to create, routing/automation rules, handoff triggers, and channel coverage — including any gaps where a channel or handoff condition isn't supported and would need a workaround.

Do not create the teams, enable the automations, or change any live settings in {{vendor}} yourself. Present the full draft configuration to me and stop for human sign-off before anything is applied. Report back with the complete checklist, any capability gaps you found, and a short summary of what will change once I approve.

growth_004:n4.prompt:
You are helping me draft help center articles for our customer support setup (using Intercom or whichever help center tool we've configured). Before starting, ask me for: (1) my product/domain name and a link or access to existing product documentation, FAQs, or support tickets to draw from; (2) the list of topics or article titles I want covered (e.g., 'How to reset your password', 'Billing FAQ', 'Refund policy'); (3) our brand voice/tone guidelines if any exist; and (4) access to the help center platform if you need to check existing article structure or categories.

Once you have these inputs, draft each article with: a clear title, a short summary/intro, step-by-step instructions or explanations, and any relevant screenshots or links I provide. Organize articles into logical categories matching our existing help center structure if one exists. Flag any topics where you're uncertain about accuracy, pricing, policy details, or edge cases — do not guess at policy specifics (refund windows, pricing tiers, legal terms) that you cannot verify from the materials I gave you.

Compile all drafted articles into a single document or list, clearly labeled by proposed category and title, ready for my review. Do not publish, upload, or push any article live to the help center. This requires a human's domain judgment on accuracy and brand alignment, so please stop for human sign-off once drafts are ready.

Report back with: the full list of drafted articles (title + body text), the proposed category structure, and a short list of open questions or uncertain claims that need my verification before publishing.

growth_004:n5.prompt:
You are helping me configure auto-responses for customer support in {{vendor}}, our AI-native support agent tool. Approval requirement: a human must explicitly approve before any changes go live, so you must prepare everything and then stop for human sign-off.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: my {{vendor}} account access (use your configured credentials), our domain/product name, common issue types we support, and any existing help center or SOPs to reference.

Then do the following, working only within {{vendor}}'s configuration interface:
1. Draft trigger rules that fire automatic actions on defined events (e.g., new ticket, tag applied, keyword detected).
2. Encode standard operating procedures as deterministic step-by-step branching flows for our known issue types, so the agent follows a consistent path rather than improvising.
3. Configure guardrails so the agent never invents policies, prices, or promises — any off-knowledge question should trigger a safe decline or handoff instead of a guess.
4. Mark sensitive topics (legal threats, cancellations, security issues) as human-only, ensuring the agent never responds automatically on these.
5. Enable supervised/draft mode so all AI-generated replies are queued for human review and approval before reaching any customer — do not enable any mode that sends replies directly to customers.

Compile a clear summary showing: the trigger rules created, the SOP branches encoded, the guardrail settings, the human-only topic list, and confirmation that supervised draft mode is active. Present this as a checklist for my review.

Do not activate, publish, or approve any of these settings yourself, and do not switch off supervised mode. Once your draft configuration and checklist are ready, stop for human sign-off and report back with the summary so I can review and approve the changes myself.

growth_004:n6.prompt:
You are helping me add team members to {{vendor}}, the customer support platform we're setting up for our helpdesk (messaging, help center, ticket management).

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available:
- The list of team members to add (name, email, and intended role/permission level for each — e.g., admin, agent, read-only)
- Confirmation of which {{vendor}} workspace/organization this applies to
- Any team or inbox groupings these members should belong to, if we use them

Then do the following:
1. Using my configured credentials, sign in to the {{vendor}} dashboard.
2. Navigate to the team/people management settings.
3. Prepare the full list of invitations, matching each person to the correct role and any team/inbox assignment, based on what I provided.
4. Check for any existing members or pending invites that might conflict or duplicate, and flag those to me.
5. Do NOT send the invitations or apply any role changes yet — this step requires my explicit approval before anything is applied.

When you're done, report back with:
- A clear summary table: name, email, proposed role, proposed team/inbox
- Any conflicts, duplicates, or ambiguous role mappings you found
- A confirmation that everything is staged and ready

Then stop for human sign-off — I will review the list and approve before you send any invitations or finalize role assignments. Do not click send, approve, or submit on my behalf under any circumstances.
